panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Coronal abdominal/pelvic CT from the reported hairy cell leukemia case visibly demonstrates massive splenomegaly extending into the pelvis, with arrows indicating the spleen. B: Sagittal abdominal/pelvic CT from the hairy cell leukemia case shows the massively enlarged spleen extending into the pelvis and compressing the bladder. C: Bone marrow H&E from the confirmed hairy cell leukemia case shows characteristic infiltrating atypical lymphocytes with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and irregular cell margins. D: CD20 immunohistochemistry confirms the B-cell identity of the atypical marrow infiltrate in this patient with hairy cell leukemia. CD20 positivity is not represented in the allowed findings vocabulary and is therefore proposed separately.

panels.figure_caption: Coronal (upper left) and sagittal (upper right) views of a noncontrast computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen/pelvis showing massive splenomegaly. The spleen can be seen extending into the pelvis with a mass effect on the bladder (white arrows). Hematoxylin and eosin staining of the bone marrow showing the characteristic infiltration by atypical lymphocytes with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and irregular margins (lower left). Immunohistochemical staining reveals the atypical lymphocytes to stain strongly positive for CD 20, confirming their origin as B cells (lower right)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Lateral abdominal CT from a patient with hairy cell leukemia demonstrates the captioned massive spleen and abnormalities concerning atraumatic splenic rupture with hemoperitoneum. B: Coronal abdominal CT shows the enlarged spleen indicated by an arrow; the disease-focused case title and caption attribute the presentation to hairy cell leukemia. C: Upper axial CT image shows the arrowed splenic abnormality in the patient with hairy cell leukemia; the caption specifically describes splenomegaly and rupture-associated findings. D: Lower axial CT image shows the arrowed enlarged spleen and associated abnormalities; the case report attributes atraumatic spontaneous splenic rupture to hairy cell leukemia.

panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography: lateral, coronal, and cross-sectional views of the abdomen with findings concerning massive splenomegaly measuring approximately 25 cm (blue arrow). Irregular hypoattenuating areas within the inferolateral and superolateral aspects of the spleen with small to moderate volume hemoperitoneum.
in_text_mentions: No fever, chills, dysuria, or gastrointestinal complaints were reported. Computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen displayed massive splenomegaly measuring approximately 25 cm with a hemoperitoneum with a high suspicion of atraumatic, spontaneous splenic rupture (Figure 1).
